01-co-loa-ngay-nay: EXCEPTION: this single scene is set in the PRESENT DAY, modern things are allowed. High wide view over the outskirts of Hanoi: green rice fields and small village houses with red-tile and concrete roofs, and running through them three long curving grassy earthen ramparts, one inside another, overgrown with trees and bamboo, the remains of an ancient citadel. A few people on motorbikes on a lane, a school, flat bright day.
02-kinh-do-au-lac: Daytime, high wide view of the ancient citadel of Cổ Loa in the 3rd century BC: three huge concentric earthen ramparts with wooden palisades on top, moats of water between them, and inside, a town of Đông Sơn stilt houses with curved boat-shaped thatched roofs, a large royal hall at the centre. Boats on the moats, people and buffalo on the paths. Green rice fields around.
03-an-duong-vuong: Medium-wide shot inside the royal hall of Cổ Loa, daytime. AN DƯƠNG VƯƠNG sits on a carved wooden throne under the curved thatched roof, calm and commanding, a bronze spear beside him. Two large Đông Sơn bronze drums flank him. A few Âu Lạc officials kneel on mats before him. Plain dark banners with no writing.
04-dap-thanh-dat: Daytime, a huge building site. Hundreds of Âu Lạc workers in loincloths and wrap skirts carry earth in pairs of baskets on shoulder poles and pound it down with wooden rammers to raise a long, tall earthen rampart. Others dig a moat beside it. Buffalo pull sledges of earth. No bricks anywhere, only earth and wood.
05-vong-thanh-ngoai: Daytime, very high bird's-eye view looking almost straight down at the three concentric rings of the Cổ Loa ramparts, the outer ring huge and curving away to the edges of the frame, tiny houses and fields between the rings, moats glinting. The scale of the outer ring is the subject.
06-thanh-lo: Daytime, a dramatic moment: a newly built section of earthen rampart is collapsing, earth sliding down in a big flat brown landslide, wooden palisade posts toppling. Âu Lạc workers jump back in alarm, dropping their baskets. AN DƯƠNG VƯƠNG stands on a rise nearby watching with a worried frown. No one is hurt.
07-kim-quy: At the edge of a calm wide river at dawn, soft golden light. KIM QUY, an enormous golden turtle, rises from the water. AN DƯƠNG VƯƠNG kneels on the bank with both hands held out, and the turtle gently places one shining golden claw into his palms. Mist on the water, reeds, a few bronze drums on the bank. Magical but calm.
08-no-than-nghi-van: Daytime inside a quiet modern museum hall. EXCEPTION: present day, modern things allowed. A large Đông Sơn crossbow model with a golden trigger piece is displayed on a plinth under soft light, with an empty glass case beside it. A couple of visitors look at it thoughtfully. A blank information panel with NO text. Calm, questioning mood.
09-kho-mui-ten-dong: Daytime at an archaeological dig beside an old earthen rampart. EXCEPTION: present day, modern things allowed. Vietnamese archaeologists in sun hats kneel in a square excavation pit with trowels and brushes, uncovering a huge heap of thousands of green-bronze three-edged arrowheads spilling out of the earth. Measuring strings, buckets, a camera on a tripod. The heap of arrowheads is the clear subject.
10-trieu-da-thua: Battle in front of the Cổ Loa ramparts, daytime. On the rampart, Âu Lạc archers shoot crossbows, the bolts drawn as thin lines falling like rain. Below, the Nam Việt army in lamellar armour with halberds and plain red banners retreats in disorder. TRIỆU ĐÀ, in armour on horseback at the rear, looks shocked. No blood, no wounds.
11-cau-hon: A formal ceremony inside the royal hall of Cổ Loa, daytime. AN DƯƠNG VƯƠNG sits on his throne. TRỌNG THỦY bows deeply before him, holding up a lacquered gift box; Nam Việt envoys in dark robes kneel behind him with more gifts. To the side, MỴ CHÂU stands shyly beside her father, glancing at the young prince. Bronze drums, curved thatched roof.
12-trao-lay: Night in light blue-grey tones lit by a single oil lamp, clearly readable. Inside a palace storeroom, MỴ CHÂU, smiling and trusting, shows TRỌNG THỦY a large crossbow resting on a stand. While she looks away at the lamp, TRỌNG THỦY secretly slips the golden trigger piece off the crossbow and hides it in his wide sleeve, an ordinary bronze trigger in his other hand ready to put in its place.
13-long-ngong: Daytime on a forest path outside the citadel. MỴ CHÂU, in her ivory tunic, walks along the path pulling small white goose feathers from a feather cloak over her arm and dropping them on the ground at a fork in the path; a trail of white feathers stretches back behind her. Bamboo and trees along the path, soft light, quiet and sad.
14-no-mat-linh: Battle at the Cổ Loa ramparts, daytime. AN DƯƠNG VƯƠNG stands on the rampart pulling the trigger of the large crossbow, but nothing happens: no bolts fly, his face shows shock. Below, the Nam Việt army with red banners and ladders surges toward the wall unstoppably. TRIỆU ĐÀ on horseback points forward. No blood.
15-au-lac-mat: Late afternoon, sombre warm light. The Cổ Loa citadel seen from a distance: Nam Việt red banners with no writing now fly over the ramparts and the royal hall, Nam Việt soldiers stand guard at the gate. Âu Lạc villagers in the foreground stand silent with heads lowered. Smoke from a few fires drifts in the sky. No bodies, no blood.
16-su-ky: Inside a Han scholar's study, daytime, window light. The old historian Tư Mã Thiên, a Han Chinese man with a grey beard in a dark robe and black cap, kneels at a low desk writing on a long bamboo-slip scroll with a brush; more bamboo scrolls are stacked on shelves behind him. The writing on the slips is drawn only as abstract short black dashes, never readable characters.
17-thanh-con-do: EXCEPTION: this single scene is set in the PRESENT DAY, modern things are allowed. Late afternoon golden light on a grassy ancient earthen rampart at Cổ Loa, tall old trees on top. A Vietnamese family, parents and two children in modern clothes, walk along the top of the rampart; the father points out over the fields. Rice fields and a village temple roof below. Peaceful, warm, hopeful.
